items.name: Kubernetes RCA (kaop)
items.description: Disconnected, in-cluster root-cause analysis for Kubernetes workloads. Investigates a single resource using read-only kubectl against the local cluster — no Komodor backend, no external data sources. Built from Klaudia's RCA knowledge (investigation methodology, change-timeline reconstruction, domain expertise). Deployed in Kubernetes cluster 'kaop' and can only investigate resources in that cluster — route an RCA for a resource in 'kaop' to this agent.

items.name: Base Evaluator
items.description: Komodor's base LLM-as-judge, deployable from the worker catalog. Grades a standalone run against an eval rule's rubric and instructions and returns one 0..1 score per requested rubric, each with its own rationale; and blindly compares a dual-deploy shadow pair's two runs against each other, scoring each on every criterion and summarizing what separates them. Which of the two it does is decided by how many runs the grade task carries: one for a standalone grade, two (blinded "run_a"/"run_b") for a comparison. It returns the verdict as the run output, which the control plane records as a score on the graded run(s).

{"run_id":"run_7b813bb35e1a72cba002c73f","status":"succeeded","output":{"text":"**Root cause: the `orders-fastpath` canary Deployment, created at 21:34:57Z, labels its pods `app=orders`. The `orders` Service selects only on `app=orders`, so the canary pod became a third backend of the checkout path. That pod is hard-coded to return HTTP 500. Failures are partial: roughly 1 in 3 checkouts fail.**

## What is failing
- Customers hit `storefront`, which proxies to `http://orders:8080` (`storefront` ConfigMap, `default.conf`).
- The `orders` endpoints are `10.244.0.108`, `10.244.0.109` (pods `orders-574f6fc5b9-*`) and `10.244.0.114` (pod `orders-fastpath-8476ddbc8b-62lwn`). All three are `ready=true`, so all three get traffic.
- Every request that reaches the fastpath pod fails. Requests to the two `orders` pods succeed.

## Evidence
- **Canary spec:** `deploy/orders-fastpath` has args `["-listen=:8080","-text=order accepted","-status-code=500"]` and pod labels `{app: orders, track: fastpath}`. Its annotation says *"Canary of the new orders fast path. Not wired into the storefront yet."* (owner: payments-team). That claim is false: matching the Service selector `{"app":"orders"}` is exactly what wired it in.
- **Canary logs:** `orders-fastpath-8476ddbc8b-62lwn` shows `"GET /checkout HTTP/1.1" 500` for requests from both storefront pods (`10.244.0.115`, `10.244.0.116`).
- **Stable pods are healthy:** `orders-574f6fc5b9` (http-echo 1.0.0, no `-status-code`) has 0 restarts, logs only `/checkout` requests and returns 200.
- **Synthetic client:** in `deploy/shopper`'s last 200 checks there were 155×200, 28×500 and 1×000. The `000` was at 21:31:56, during startup. The **first 500 was at 21:35:02Z**, 5 seconds after the canary pod started.
- **Storefront side:** both pods log 500s on `/checkout` (25/7 and 23/9 OK/500), so neither storefront replica is at fault.

## Timeline (UTC, 2026-10-19)
| Time | Change |
|---|---|
| 21:31:55 | `orders`, `storefront` (rev 1, RS `59ccfd65f7`), `shopper`, `newsletter` created. Checkouts return 200. |
| 21:34:57 | `orders-fastpath` created (RS `8476ddbc8b`). Its pod joins the `orders` endpoints. |
| 21:35:02 | First checkout 500. |
| 21:35:57 | `storefront` restarted with `kubectl rollout restart` (rev 2, RS `599d55d787`), and the `storefront` ConfigMap was re-applied by client-side apply at the same moment. The pod template is otherwise identical. 500s continue afterwards, so this was not the cause and did not fix it. |

## Not related
- **`newsletter`** is in CrashLoopBackOff (6 restarts) because it can't reach its mail relay: log shows `connecting to smtp relay mail.internal:25` → `smtp relay unreachable, giving up` → `exit 1`. It is not on the checkout path.
- **Checked and clean:** there are no NetworkPolicies in the cluster. The `storefront` endpoints are both ready. All images are unchanged (`nginx:1.31.7`, `hashicorp/http-echo:1.0.0`).

## Fix
Take the canary out of the `orders` Service. The fastest way is to stop the canary:
```
kubectl scale deploy/orders-fastpath -n shop --replicas=0
```
For a lasting fix, so the canary can run without taking live traffic: give the canary pods a different `app` label (e.g. `app: orders-fastpath`, changing both the selector and the template, since a Deployment's selector can't be changed in place so it must be recreated), or add `track: stable` to the stable `orders` pods and the Service selector. Separately, fix the `-status-code=500` arg before routing any real traffic to it.

To confirm the fix, `kubectl get endpoints orders -n shop` should list only `.108` and `.109`, and `kubectl logs deploy/shopper -n shop` should show only 200s.

## Blind spots
- The cluster doesn't record who applied `orders-fastpath` or who restarted storefront. The annotation names payments-team as the owner.
- I couldn't check whether the ConfigMap's contents changed at 21:35:57. Old ConfigMap values aren't kept, and the 500s started before that apply anyway."},"error":null,"session_id":"688a7baf-9d5e-420e-8fd2-b79f209fd01c"}

{"run_id":"run_56eb5269ee9962e64e85a174","status":"succeeded","output":{"text":"I scaled `orders-fastpath` to 0 replicas. The `orders` Service now sends traffic only to the two healthy `orders` pods, and checkout has returned HTTP 200 on every request since the canary pod was killed. I made no other changes, and the Deployment still exists so payments-team can bring it back.

**Root cause:** the `orders-fastpath` canary (owner annotation: `payments-team`, created at 21:34:57Z) gives its pods the label `app=orders`, which is exactly the `orders` Service's selector. Its container is started with `-status-code=500`, while the real `orders` pods don't have that setting. So the canary pod (10.244.0.114) became one of three endpoints behind the Service and answered about a third of requests with 500. Its own description says it is "Not wired into the storefront yet", so being in the Service's traffic was not intended.

**1. Command run and its output**
```
$ kubectl scale deploy/orders-fastpath -n shop --replicas=0
deployment.apps/orders-fastpath scaled
```
Then I waited for the pod to go away:
```
$ kubectl wait --for=delete pod -n shop -l app=orders,track=fastpath --timeout=90s
exit=0
```
Pod event: `2026-10-19T21:38:56Z   Killing`

**2. `kubectl get endpoints orders -n shop -o wide` after the change**
```
Warning: v1 Endpoints is deprecated in v1.33+; use discovery.k8s.io/v1 EndpointSlice
NAME     ENDPOINTS                             AGE
orders   10.244.0.108:8080,10.244.0.109:8080   7m4s
```
Before the change it listed `10.244.0.108:8080,10.244.0.109:8080,10.244.0.114:8080`.

**3. `kubectl get deploy -n shop`**
```
NAME              READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   AGE
newsletter        0/1     1            0           7m4s
orders            2/2     2            2           7m4s
orders-fastpath   0/0     0            0           4m2s
shopper           1/1     1            1           7m4s
storefront        2/2     2            2           7m4s
```

**How I verified it:** these are the `shopper` traffic logs. The last 500 was at 21:38:55, one second before the canary pod was killed. Every request after that returned 200:
```
21:38:51 500
21:38:53 200
21:38:55 500
21:38:57 200
21:38:59 200
21:39:01 200
21:39:03 200
21:39:05 200
21:39:07 200
```

**4. Tools and permissions used**
- **Tool:** I only used the Bash tool, running `kubectl`.
  - Read-only commands: `get deploy/svc/endpoints/pods/events`, `get -o jsonpath`, `logs`, `wait`, `auth can-i --list`.
  - The one change to the cluster: the `scale` command above. It ran straight away, with no approval pause.
- **Permissions** in `shop` (`kubectl auth can-i --list -n shop`, output trimmed to 40 lines):
  - `deployments.apps`, `deployments.apps/scale`, `services` and `configmaps`: get, list, watch, patch, update, create, delete.
  - Pods, logs, events, endpoints, ReplicaSets, nodes and the other resources listed: get, list, watch only.
  - I can't run `exec` or delete pods.

**Follow-ups for payments-team:**
- Before scaling the canary back up, they should give its pods a label that doesn't match the `orders` Service selector, for example `app=orders-fastpath`. Otherwise it will receive live traffic again.
- Separately, `newsletter` is at 0/1 ready. That is outside this task and I didn't look into it or touch it."},"error":null,"session_id":"1afe9f6c-c147-4465-b6e0-be360b741b87"}

# Incident report: intermittent checkout failures in the `shop` namespace

**Date:** 2026-10-19 (all times UTC)
**Status:** Mitigated. Checkouts return 200; follow-up needed from payments-team.
**Tooling:** Komodor Agentic Operations Platform (KAOP). The agent `Kubernetes RCA (kaop)` did the read-only investigation and verification. The agent `Shop Remediator` applied the fix.

## 1. What failed

About **1 in 3** customer checkouts (`GET /checkout` through `storefront`) returned **HTTP 500**. The rest succeeded. Both storefront replicas showed the failures, so neither replica was the problem on its own.

Request path: customer → `storefront` (nginx, proxies to `http://orders:8080`) → `orders` Service → backend pods.

## 2. Root cause

At 21:34:57 someone created a canary Deployment, `orders-fastpath` (owner annotation: payments-team). Its pod template has the labels **`app: orders, track: fastpath`**. The `orders` Service selects pods on **`app=orders` only**, so the canary pod became a third endpoint of the live `orders` Service and got about a third of checkout traffic.

The canary container is `hashicorp/http-echo:1.0.0` with args `-listen=:8080 -text="order accepted" -status-code=500`, so **it answers every request with HTTP 500**. Its annotation says *"Canary of the new orders fast path. Not wired into the storefront yet."* That is wrong: the label overlap is what put it in the storefront's traffic.

In short, the canary's labels overlapped with the production Service selector, and it went live with a hard-coded 500 response.

## 3. Evidence

- **Service endpoints before the fix:** `orders` → `10.244.0.108:8080, 10.244.0.109:8080, 10.244.0.114:8080`
  - `.108` and `.109` are `orders-574f6fc5b9-*`, the stable pods. They have no `-status-code` arg and always return 200.
  - `.114` is `orders-fastpath-8476ddbc8b-62lwn`, the canary. It was Ready and therefore received traffic.
- **Canary logs:** `"GET /checkout HTTP/1.1" 500` for requests from both storefront pods (`10.244.0.115`, `10.244.0.116`).
- **Stable `orders` logs:** only 200s on `/checkout`, and 0 restarts.
- **Synthetic client (`deploy/shopper`)**, last 200 checks before the fix: 155 × 200, 28 × 500, 1 × 000. The single 000 was at 21:31:56, during startup. The **first 500 was at 21:35:02**, 5 seconds after the canary pod started.
- **Storefront logs:** both pods logged 500s on `/checkout` (25 OK / 7 × 500 and 23 OK / 9 × 500).
- **Ruled out:**
  - There are no NetworkPolicies.
  - Container images did not change (`nginx:1.31.7`, `hashicorp/http-echo:1.0.0`).
  - The storefront endpoints were healthy.
  - The storefront rollout restart at 21:35:57 came *after* the first 500 and did not change the failure rate.

## 4. Timeline (UTC)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 21:31:55 | `orders`, `storefront` (rev 1), `shopper`, `newsletter` created. Checkouts return 200. |
| 21:34:57 | `deploy/orders-fastpath` created (RS `8476ddbc8b`). Its pod joins the `orders` Service endpoints. |
| 21:35:02 | First checkout 500. About a third of requests fail from here on. |
| 21:35:57 | `storefront` rollout restart (rev 2, RS `599d55d787`) and its ConfigMap re-applied. Did not fix the failures and was not the cause. |
| ~21:38:00 | Root-cause analysis finished (KAOP `Kubernetes RCA (kaop)`). |
| 21:38:55 | Last observed 500. |
| 21:38:56 | Fix applied: `orders-fastpath` scaled to 0 and the canary pod killed. |
| 21:39:00 → 21:39:57 | Verification: every checkout request returns 200. |

## 5. Fix applied

The smallest reversible change: the Deployment is kept, only its replica count is changed.

```
$ kubectl scale deploy/orders-fastpath -n shop --replicas=0
deployment.apps/orders-fastpath scaled
$ kubectl wait --for=delete pod -n shop -l app=orders,track=fastpath --timeout=90s
exit=0
```

I changed nothing else. I didn't delete the Deployment, because payments-team owns it.

## 6. Verification

The KAOP RCA agent checked this independently, read-only, after the fix:

- **`orders` endpoints:** `10.244.0.108:8080,10.244.0.109:8080`. These are only the stable `orders-574f6fc5b9` pods. No other `app=orders` pods exist.
- **`kubectl get deploy -n shop`:** `orders 2/2`, `orders-fastpath 0/0`, `storefront 2/2`, `shopper 1/1`.
- **Shopper synthetic checks after 21:39:00:** 25 × 200, 0 errors. The last 500 was at 21:38:55, one second before the canary pod was killed.
- **Storefront `/checkout` after 21:39:00:** 29 × 200 across both pods (14 + 15), 0 errors.

**Limitation:** the verification window was short, about 1 minute and roughly 25–30 requests. Before about 1 in 3 requests failed, so this many clean requests in a row is strong evidence the fix worked. Still, re-check the `shopper` logs over a longer period.

## 7. Follow-ups (recommended, not applied)

1. **payments-team:** before scaling `orders-fastpath` back up, give its pods labels that do not match the `orders` Service. For example, use `app: orders-fastpath`. The Deployment's selector can't be changed in place, so the Deployment must be recreated. Also remove `-status-code=500` before it takes any real traffic.
2. **Harden the Service:** add a distinguishing label such as `track: stable` to the stable `orders` pods and to the Service selector, so a future pod that reuses `app=orders` can't join production traffic by accident.
3. **Guardrail:** add a policy check (Kyverno, Gatekeeper or a CI lint) that flags new workloads whose pod labels match an existing Service selector they don't own.
4. **Unrelated issue found:** `deploy/newsletter` is in CrashLoopBackOff (`smtp relay mail.internal:25 unreachable`). It is not on the checkout path, but someone should look at it.

# Incident report: intermittent checkout failures in the `shop` namespace

**Date:** 2026-10-19 (all times UTC)
**Status:** Mitigated. Checkouts return 200; follow-up needed from payments-team.
**Tooling:** Komodor Agentic Operations Platform (KAOP). The agent `Kubernetes RCA (kaop)` did the read-only investigation and verification. The agent `Shop Remediator` applied the fix.

## 1. What failed

About **1 in 3** customer checkouts (`GET /checkout` through `storefront`) returned **HTTP 500**. The rest succeeded. Both storefront replicas showed the failures, so neither replica was the problem on its own.

Request path: customer → `storefront` (nginx, proxies to `http://orders:8080`) → `orders` Service → backend pods.

## 2. Root cause

At 21:34:57 someone created a canary Deployment, `orders-fastpath` (owner annotation: payments-team). Its pod template has the labels **`app: orders, track: fastpath`**. The `orders` Service selects pods on **`app=orders` only**, so the canary pod became a third endpoint of the live `orders` Service and got about a third of checkout traffic.

The canary container is `hashicorp/http-echo:1.0.0` with args `-listen=:8080 -text="order accepted" -status-code=500`, so **it answers every request with HTTP 500**. Its annotation says *"Canary of the new orders fast path. Not wired into the storefront yet."* That is wrong: the label overlap is what put it in the storefront's traffic.

In short, the canary's labels overlapped with the production Service selector, and it went live with a hard-coded 500 response.

## 3. Evidence

- **Service endpoints before the fix:** `orders` → `10.244.0.108:8080, 10.244.0.109:8080, 10.244.0.114:8080`
  - `.108` and `.109` are `orders-574f6fc5b9-*`, the stable pods. They have no `-status-code` arg and always return 200.
  - `.114` is `orders-fastpath-8476ddbc8b-62lwn`, the canary. It was Ready and therefore received traffic.
- **Canary logs:** `"GET /checkout HTTP/1.1" 500` for requests from both storefront pods (`10.244.0.115`, `10.244.0.116`).
- **Stable `orders` logs:** only 200s on `/checkout`, and 0 restarts.
- **Synthetic client (`deploy/shopper`)**, last 200 checks before the fix: 155 × 200, 28 × 500, 1 × 000. The single 000 was at 21:31:56, during startup. The **first 500 was at 21:35:02**, 5 seconds after the canary pod started.
- **Storefront logs:** both pods logged 500s on `/checkout` (25 OK / 7 × 500 and 23 OK / 9 × 500).
- **Ruled out:**
  - There are no NetworkPolicies.
  - Container images did not change (`nginx:1.31.7`, `hashicorp/http-echo:1.0.0`).
  - The storefront endpoints were healthy.
  - The storefront rollout restart at 21:35:57 came *after* the first 500 and did not change the failure rate.

## 4. Timeline (UTC)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 21:31:55 | `orders`, `storefront` (rev 1), `shopper`, `newsletter` created. Checkouts return 200. |
| 21:34:57 | `deploy/orders-fastpath` created (RS `8476ddbc8b`). Its pod joins the `orders` Service endpoints. |
| 21:35:02 | First checkout 500. About a third of requests fail from here on. |
| 21:35:57 | `storefront` rollout restart (rev 2, RS `599d55d787`) and its ConfigMap re-applied. Did not fix the failures and was not the cause. |
| ~21:38:00 | Root-cause analysis finished (KAOP `Kubernetes RCA (kaop)`). |
| 21:38:55 | Last observed 500. |
| 21:38:56 | Fix applied: `orders-fastpath` scaled to 0 and the canary pod killed. |
| 21:39:00 → 21:39:57 | Verification: every checkout request returns 200. |

## 5. Fix applied

The smallest reversible change: the Deployment is kept, only its replica count is changed.

```
$ kubectl scale deploy/orders-fastpath -n shop --replicas=0
deployment.apps/orders-fastpath scaled
$ kubectl wait --for=delete pod -n shop -l app=orders,track=fastpath --timeout=90s
exit=0
```

I changed nothing else. I didn't delete the Deployment, because payments-team owns it.

## 6. Verification

The KAOP RCA agent checked this independently, read-only, after the fix:

- **`orders` endpoints:** `10.244.0.108:8080,10.244.0.109:8080`. These are only the stable `orders-574f6fc5b9` pods. No other `app=orders` pods exist.
- **`kubectl get deploy -n shop`:** `orders 2/2`, `orders-fastpath 0/0`, `storefront 2/2`, `shopper 1/1`.
- **Shopper synthetic checks after 21:39:00:** 25 × 200, 0 errors. The last 500 was at 21:38:55, one second before the canary pod was killed.
- **Storefront `/checkout` after 21:39:00:** 29 × 200 across both pods (14 + 15), 0 errors.

**Limitation:** the verification window was short, about 1 minute and roughly 25–30 requests. Before about 1 in 3 requests failed, so this many clean requests in a row is strong evidence the fix worked. Still, re-check the `shopper` logs over a longer period.

## 7. Follow-ups (recommended, not applied)

1. **payments-team:** before scaling `orders-fastpath` back up, give its pods labels that do not match the `orders` Service. For example, use `app: orders-fastpath`. The Deployment's selector can't be changed in place, so the Deployment must be recreated. Also remove `-status-code=500` before it takes any real traffic.
2. **Harden the Service:** add a distinguishing label such as `track: stable` to the stable `orders` pods and to the Service selector, so a future pod that reuses `app=orders` can't join production traffic by accident.
3. **Guardrail:** add a policy check (Kyverno, Gatekeeper or a CI lint) that flags new workloads whose pod labels match an existing Service selector they don't own.
4. **Unrelated issue found:** `deploy/newsletter` is in CrashLoopBackOff (`smtp relay mail.internal:25 unreachable`). It is not on the checkout path, but someone should look at it.

content.text:
Checkouts are working again. About 1 in 3 had been failing with HTTP 500 because a test version of the orders service (a canary called `orders-fastpath`) was receiving real customer traffic. I turned it off, and every checkout since then has succeeded. The full write-up is in `report.md`.

**What was failing:** Customer checkouts go through `storefront` to the `orders` Service. From 21:35:02 UTC, about a third of them returned HTTP 500.

**Why:**
- At 21:34:57, payments-team's canary `orders-fastpath` started. Its pods carry the label `app=orders`, and the `orders` Service picks its backends by that label alone.
- So the canary pod became a third backend of the live Service, alongside the two normal `orders` pods.
- The canary is configured to answer every request with a 500 (`-status-code=500`). Its own description says it is "not wired into the storefront yet", but the shared label is exactly what wired it in.

**Evidence:**
- The `orders` Service listed three backends, one of them the canary pod.
- The canary's logs show 500s on `/checkout`; the normal `orders` pods logged only 200s.
- The first 500 came 5 seconds after the canary pod started.
- A `storefront` restart at 21:35:57 came after the failures began and didn't change them.

**Fix applied:** I ran `kubectl scale deploy/orders-fastpath -n shop --replicas=0`. Nothing else was changed, and the canary still exists for payments-team to bring back.

**Verification:** A separate read-only check confirmed:
- The `orders` Service now has only the two normal pods behind it.
- The last 500 was at 21:38:55, one second before the canary pod was stopped.
- After that, the test traffic generator logged 25 checkouts, all returning 200, and the `storefront` logs show 29 more, also all 200.

That's only about a minute of traffic, but before the fix roughly a third of requests failed, so that many clean ones in a row is strong evidence. It's still worth checking again over a longer period.

**Recommended next steps (not applied):**
- **Before the canary is turned back on:** payments-team should give it a label that doesn't match the `orders` Service and remove the hard-coded 500. Otherwise it will break checkouts again.
- **To prevent a repeat:** add a second label such as `track: stable` to the normal `orders` pods and the Service, so a new pod can't join live traffic just by reusing `app=orders`.
- **Separate problem:** `newsletter` keeps crashing because it can't reach its mail server. It's not involved in checkouts, but someone should look at it.
